sheet.title: Happy Thanksgiving from Brennan’s, 3 Courses $80: choice of appetizer, entrée and dessert
sheet.line: Popcorn Rice Pilaf, Pickled Peppers, Creole Tomato Gravy
sheet.note: The sheet prints the dish name and its line and nothing else: no allergen marks, no price of its own (the $80 covers three courses), no method, no portion, no wine.

classic.piquante: Sauce piquante is a hot, tomato based Louisiana dish served over rice, built on a roux with onion, bell pepper, celery and garlic, smothering whatever meat or seafood is on hand: chicken, catfish, turtle, rabbit, alligator or shrimp; it has long been popular in Acadiana (Rouses Markets, The Sauce For Whatever You Caught; Wikipedia, Cajun cuisine; Atlas Obscura, Turtle sauce picante). No documented origin or date was found, so none is given.
classic.tomatoGravy: Southern tomato gravy is a roux with tomatoes and a little liquid; it is not New Orleans red gravy, the Sicilian rooted tomato sauce (MasterClass, Tomato Gravy; AOL, What Is Tomato Gravy?). The sheet’s Creole tomato gravy is not defined anywhere; the notes say only tomato gravy and send the rest to the kitchen.
classic.pilaf: A pilaf is rice cooked in fat before its liquid goes in, so the grains stay separate; the pack’s popcorn rice component already explains the Louisiana aromatic rice.

sayIt: Sauce piquante: sohs pee-KAHNT; piquant is French for sharp or pungent.
unsourced: How hot the kitchen’s sauce piquante runs, what peppers are pickled, and what goes into the Creole tomato gravy: asked of the chef.
A date or a founder for sauce piquante: none documented.
